title: Azure Managed Disk Performance Throttling

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.57 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.57 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:monitor:metric` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.compute/disks"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.57_azure_managed_disk_perfo_57"
| sort -_time
description: Azure managed disks have IOPS and throughput caps based on tier and size. When VMs hit these limits, disk I/O is throttled, causing application slowdowns that are hard to diagnose without platform metrics.
value: Detecting azure managed disk performance throttling early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Collect Azure Monitor metrics for managed disks. Monitor `Composite Disk Read/Write IOPS` against the disk SKU IOPS limit and `Composite Disk Read/Write Bytes/sec` against the throughput limit. For burstable disks, track `BurstIOCreditsConsumedPercentage` — when credits exhaust, performance drops to baseline. Alert when consumption exceeds 90% of provisioned capacity sustained over 15 minutes.
visualization: Gauge (IOPS vs. limit), Line chart (throughput and burst credits), Table (disks hitting limits).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.storage_free_percent) as free_pct
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.Storage
  by Performance.host span=1h
| sort 10 free_pct
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (Storage node).

references.title: Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform

knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics) with the modular input for `azure:monitor:metric`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect Azure Monitor metrics for managed disks. Monitor `Composite Disk Read/Write IOPS` against the disk SKU IOPS limit and `Composite Disk Read/Write Bytes/sec` against the throughput limit. For burstable disks, track `BurstIOCreditsConsumedPercentage` — when credits exhaust, performance drops to baseline. Alert when consumption exceeds 90% of provisioned capacity sustained over 15 minutes.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.compute/disks"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.57_azure_managed_disk_perfo_57"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:monitor:metric` in `index=cloud` to detect azure managed disk performance throttling. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_57_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Gauge (IOPS vs. limit), Line chart (throughput and burst credits), Table (disks hitting limits)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure managed disk performance throttling so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
